html:<span class=\"tag h\">真实数据 · 训练好的控制: html:Real data · trained controller · hand-written transitionsFlight is performed in a MuJoCo physics simulation by the trained flight controller published with the flybody paper (Vaxenburg et al. 2025 Nature, figshare trained-fly-policies/flight): the controller follows recordings of real fruit-fly escape flights (Muijres et al. 2014 Science, raw trajectories only), and the body position and attitude are simulation results. Median tracking error is about 0.3 mm and body orientation about 4–6°; the left-turn clip diverges to 7 mm in its last ~30 ms. The wings beat according to the controller's actual output: the controller sets the wingbeat frequency (about 219–221 Hz) and adds a correction force to each joint of the left and right wings; the real wing angles are computed by the physics engine, so left and right are no longer perfectly synchronised (left–right correlation of roll angle 0.52–0.59). Takeoff and landing are still hand-written transitions (takeoff rises 5 mm in 20 ms; after the flight, a 50 ms linear descent): no publicly downloadable fruit-fly takeoff kinematics were found, and the Card lab's FlyPEZ takeoff tracking data are available only on request from the authors. Takeoff direction is set away from the threat following Card & Dickinson 2008: a threat on the left selects the right-turn trajectory. Flight is not controlled by the connectome.
html:「生活」模式的果蝇现在用子回路 v5（<span id=\"lnN\": html:The fly in "Life" mode now uses sub-circuit v5 () = v4 + the connectome's mushroom-body learning circuit: olfactory receptor neurons → projection neurons → Kenyon cells → mushroom-body output neurons (MBONs), plus dopaminergic neurons (PAM, PPL1) and the global inhibitory APL. All wiring comes from FlyWire; the only thing that changes is the Kenyon cell → MBON synapse layer: if a Kenyon cell has just fired and there is dopamine in the same compartment, that synapse is depressed (the site and rule of fruit-fly olfactory memory in the literature: Hige 2015; Cohn 2015; Handler 2019). Which dopaminergic neuron governs which compartment is determined by the DAN → MBON synapse counts in the connectome; we did not write a lookup table. Every table below is measured, and every criterion was written before the run. To see this fly on the 3D basketball court: switch the "Brain" toggle at the top of the "Court" controls to "All five senses" — same fly, same memory, with odours, heat sources and sounds drawn on the court and each of the six legs walking in its own phase; missions, mutants and optogenetics still belong to the 5,563-neuron court version (the published numbers were measured on it).
html:<b>② 「推理 N 步」也是训练出来的，不是下棋时现算的。</b>数: html:② "Reason N steps" is also trained, not computed during play. Every position in the dataset is labelled with the best move from searching ahead 1–6 and 8 steps; for each N, one readout layer is trained with that as the label. The reasoning steps setting above the board simply selects which one to use — during play there is only model inference: line pattern → the fly brain's firing → this readout layer → the point with the highest move score, with no search at all. You can switch at any time; the move being considered is immediately rethought with the new one. The board shows its thinking: orange circles = the probability the model assigns to each candidate point, numbered ghost stones = its anticipated continuation (the same model plays N moves for both sides in turn). ③ Forbidden moves and wins are judged by the rules engine. After each move, the page reruns that move's line patterns live in the real brain and compares them with the value table — at that point the spike plot, descending neurons and sensory input on the left show the firing of the fly playing Gomoku. ④ The external search (off by default) is the alpha-beta algorithm: it is given the same value table and searches ahead, knowing only the rules and no shape scores. It is much stronger, but that is the algorithm's credit, and the page labels it separately.
html:<b>① 每条线值多少——果蝇脑 + 一层线性读出。</b>对一个候选: html:① What each line is worth — the fly brain + one linear readout layer. For a candidate point, take one line in each of 4 directions (4 cells on each side, each cell = empty / mine / opponent / edge). There are only 14,641 such line patterns, few enough that this 5,563-neuron fly brain runs every one of them: 8 cells × 3 states = 24 channels, each wired to about 61 real sensory neurons, Poisson-driven for 300 ms; spikes of downstream neurons are counted and averaged over 3 random seeds. Not a single synapse in the brain is trained; only one linear readout layer is trained, converting the firing into the line's log value. Move score = the sum of the values of 4 attack lines + λ × 4 defence lines.
html:<b>玩法像「我的世界」：</b>场景底部的工具栏（数字键选、点地面用: html:It plays like Minecraft: the toolbar at the bottom of the scene (select with number keys, click the ground to use) lets you place fruit, dig puddles, place stones, plant mushrooms / berry bushes / flowers, place beetles, raise / lower terrain and remove things — all edits act on the same world object, a placed stone really blocks the way, and edits are saved locally per seed. The world has four biomes: meadow / understorey / gravel beach / wetland. C switches the camera (orbit / follow behind / first person); holding A D S Space = directly drives the real steering / backing-up / giant fibre neurons (you are remote-controlling neurons, not the body); F fills the window with the scene and renders the brain and live spikes in the same 3D view.
html:<b>那为什么不用摄像机？</b>——那条路本来就有：<code>ey: html:So why not use a camera? — That path already exists: eyecam uses a cube-map camera to render the whole 3D scene from the fly's head, with walls, stands and other flies all included, and any object added to the court later will be included automatically. The new horizontal bar in the compound-eye window at top left is its raw projection (before it is sampled into 721 ommatidia). Measured: it does see the wall (reads a constant 0 when still, and responds as soon as it walks), but "walking towards the wall" (LPLC2 median 34.2 Hz) and "walking away from the wall" (23.5 Hz) are barely distinguishable — what it reads is mainly the whole-field optic flow caused by walking itself. Real flies have halteres and efference copies to cancel self-motion; this model has neither.
html:<b>哪些是手写的：</b>① 触角叶局部神经元一律取抑制性（递质符号: html:What is hand-written: ① all antennal-lobe local neurons are taken as inhibitory (a correction of transmitter sign, supported by the literature); ② edges touching the mushroom body keep only those with ≥2 synapses (the page cannot hold all 1.29 million); ③ the sugar / heat → dopamine wire (the connectome cannot itself activate the dopaminergic neurons, see ②); ④ the three numbers of the plasticity rule (learning rate, eligibility trace 200 ms, no forgetting); ⑤ odour A / B are synthetic (20 glomeruli each), not receptor profiles of real odours; ⑥ the mapping from descending neurons → "step frequency + left/right stride length", and the phase coupling between the six legs — the ventral nerve cord connectome cannot produce a tripod gait (the "Ventral nerve cord" section above); ⑦ the "memory → steering bridge" is entirely hand-written, so it is off by default.
html:<b>关于颜色</b>：果蝇有色觉，而且比人多一维——R7 是紫外（p: html:About colour: fruit flies have colour vision, with one more dimension than humans — R7 is ultraviolet (pale-type Rh3 ~345 nm / yellow-type Rh4 ~375 nm), R8 is blue (Rh5 ~437 nm) or green (Rh6 ~508 nm), but they can barely see red. Ommatidia come in pale / yellow types, with a measured ratio of 216 : 505 ≈ 30% : 70%, matching real flies. The second panel is coloured by this type: blue cells are pale (blue channel), green cells are yellow (green channel), like the colour mosaic of a Bayer filter. Try the "colour blocks" preset — the red block looks almost black to the fly.
html:顶部第三个标签。这是<b>单独的一只</b>果蝇，用的是新裁的子回路: html:The third tab at the top. This is a separate fly, using the newly pruned sub-circuit v4 (), which has hearing, two glomeruli (vinegar / geosmin) and 4 interoceptive neurons beyond the court fly. The world runs by itself — day and night, rotting fruit, puddles, odours, buzzing, heat sources, wind, dust, incoming balls — and each is delivered only as a physical quantity to the corresponding receptors; there is not a single "smell it and go there", "hear it and run" or "stuck, so turn around" rule. So the table below is not a feature list but a measurement: whether each sense actually reaches behaviour in this model.
html:<b>这就是那条原则的完整答案</b>：只给物理量、不写判断逻辑<b>: html:This is the full answer to that principle: giving only physical quantities without writing decision logic is feasible — once touch is delivered to the head bristles, the number of cells the fly visits rises from 9 to 31.5 and the distance travelled from 156 mm to 603 mm, with no decision of ours in between. But the precondition is that the pathway actually exists in the sub-circuit; delivering it to the wrong place (JO) is the same as giving nothing. The game page still runs v2 + that hand-written "can see the fence", because switching to v3 would require remeasuring all published missions, mutants and knockout ratios — an engineering trade-off, not a scientific conclusion.
html:<span class=\"tag c\">连接组</span>当前子: html:ConnectomeThe current sub-circuit has 4,599 neurons and 338,837 connections: all paths of at most 3 hops with ≥ 3 synapses between LC4/LPLC2/LC16/sugar/bitter/JO and DNa01, DNa02, the giant fibre, MN9, aDN1 and MDN (chosen from 3 candidate sets by the pre-set rule "≤ 6 MB, ≥ 3× real time, smallest mean deviation"). Neuron parameters are the same as in the Shiu et al. 2024 whole-brain model, dt = 0.1 ms, computed step by step in your browser.
html:舞台下方「动脑子」那一排，对应论文（Shiu et al. 2024）: html:The "Brain tweaks" row below the stage corresponds to controls the paper (Shiu et al. 2024) itself ran. Shuffle wiring is Supplementary Table 1D: keep each neuron's out-degree and its string of weights, and only randomly permute the postsynaptic targets — once the wiring is scrambled, the signal from sugar taste to the proboscis motor neuron MN9 almost entirely disappears. The weight / inhibition sliders are Supplementary Tables 11B–E (the paper uses ±30%), and glutamate made excitatory is Table 11F (the default model treats glutamate as inhibitory; the sub-circuit has 635 glutamatergic neurons, 13.8%).
html:「抽一只突变体」会随机敲掉十个真实神经元中的一个而不告诉你是哪个，你靠: html:"Draw a mutant" randomly knocks out one of ten real neurons without telling you which, and you diagnose it by feeding sugar, feeding water, dropping dust and throwing balls. But before building this game mode we had to answer one question: are these knockouts actually visible in behaviour? node dodge/mutant_test.js ran each one for 60 seconds × 3 seeds, measuring all six metrics, and "diagnosable" uses the most conservative criterion — the range of that metric over the three runs does not overlap at all with the three runs without knockout.

Takeoff when the giant fibre's 20 ms smoothed firing rate exceeds 90 Hz.
html:<b>它们的共同套路</b>：①把像素亮度灌进 R1–R6 光感受器；: html:Their common recipe: ① pour pixel brightness into the R1–R6 photoreceptors; ② hand-pick a few descending neurons as buttons (left–right difference steers, some DN goes forward, DNp01 triggers a jump); ③ add a trained network at the readout end (CEM / ridge regression / backpropagation). The third is the crux — once the readout layer is flexible enough, it becomes impossible to say whether the connectome is actually doing anything.

html:两个诚实的限制：<b>紫外无法从照片恢复</b>（sRGB 里根本没有: html:Two honest limitations: ultraviolet cannot be recovered from a photo (sRGB contains no ultraviolet at all, and that is one of the fly's most important channels); flyvis takes only one scalar per ommatidium (it was trained on an optic-flow task and has no colour channels), so colour is necessarily collapsed to one dimension at the step where it enters the neural network — the later panels are black and white because of a limitation of the model, not of the fly.
html:<strong>冗余光看连线图预测不出来。</strong>事先声明的: html:Redundancy cannot be predicted from the wiring diagram alone. The pre-registered hypothesis (backing each other up = taking separate paths) gave measured correlation coefficients of −0.008 / +0.013 — that is, zero. To know whether two neurons back each other up, you have to actually knock them out together and run it.
